messages.subject: [statnet_help] Interpretation of curved model terms if MPLE is used
messages.subject_clean: [statnet_help] Interpretation of curved model terms if MPLE is used
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

How can I interpret curved model terms like GWESP if I fit an ergm using 
MPLE and if the alpha value is not fixed? I noticed that no alpha value 
is reported. I guess the parameter is not estimated? If not, what fixed 
parameter is used? Here is a minimal example comparing MCMC and MPLE - 
MLE has 3 and MPLE has 2 parameters:

library(ergm)
mat <- matrix(rbinom(100, 1, .25), nrow = 10, ncol = 10)
diag(mat) <- 0
nw <- network(mat)
fit.mle <- ergm(nw ~ edges + gwesp, estimate = "MLE")
summary(fit.mle)
fit.mple <- ergm(nw ~ edges + gwesp, estimate = "MPLE")
summary(fit.mple)

Thanks,

Philip

messages.body_plain:
Hi, Philip.  Just to add to what Martina said:  That will work for the MLE, but for the MPLE it's more subtle.  In fact, the value of alpha is zero--the default.  Observe:

> data(faux.mesa.high)
> ergm(faux.mesa.high~gwesp, estimate="MPLE")

MPLE Coefficients:
  gwesp  
-0.4868  
> ergm(faux.mesa.high~gwesp(alpha=0), estimate="MPLE")

MPLE Coefficients:
  gwesp  
-0.4868  


Bottom line, there is no implementation for a meaningful MPLE for alpha when fixed=FALSE is used.  Perhaps we could give a warning in this case, but trying to anticipate all possibilities where such a warning should be issued is probably too difficult.  Maybe the best thing for us to do is to add "alpha=0" to the documentation so it's clearer what the default is.

Best,
Dave

messages.body_plain:
Great, this answers my question. Thanks very much. I think adding alpha 
= 0 to the documentation would be helpful. And it would be nice if MPLE 
and MCMC MLE reported the same coefficients (either with or without the 
fixed alpha value listed as a coefficient. In the current 
implementation, fixed alpha parameters are reported as coefficients by 
the MLE but not by the MPLE. This causes trouble in my case because I am 
using the simulate function to simulate new networks from an MPLE-based 
ERGM including a gwesp term. I think the problem is that 
coef.sublength.model() counts one more term than is actually present 
because it assumes that the alpha parameter is listed under coef, and 
thus the simulate function throws an error. Can you confirm this?

Philip

messages.body_plain:
Hi, Philip.  I'm not sure I fully understand:  I don't believe that an alpha value is reported by MLE when fixed=TRUE, only when fixed=FALSE.  But when MPLE is used, fixed=FALSE makes no sense.  In other words, for fixed=TRUE, both methods produce the same number of coefficients; whereas for fixed=FALSE, MPLE should not be used.

I think that maybe the confusion only arises when fixed=FALSE is used with MPLE.  I see your point that it might be helpful to have one additional coefficient output in that case, namely the (actually fixed!) value of alpha.  But it seems this might encourage the use of fixed=FALSE with MPLE, which is probably not good.

Sorry if I'm misunderstanding something!

Dave

PS.  I added alpha=0 to the documentation, so that should show up with the next release of ergm.

messages.body_plain:
Hi Dave,

You are right that MLE with fixed = TRUE produces only one coefficient. 
However, consider the following example:

library(ergm)
data(faux.mesa.high)

test1 <- ergm(faux.mesa.high ~ gwesp(alpha = 0), estimate="MPLE")
sim <- simulate(test1)  # throws an error

test2 <- ergm(faux.mesa.high ~ gwesp(alpha = 0, fixed = TRUE), 
estimate="MPLE")
sim <- simulate(test2)  # works fine

The error message is:

coef has 1 elements, while the model requires 2 parameters.

Thanks,
Philip

Dear=20statnet=20community,

I=20am=20interested=20in=20a=20kind=20of=20selective=20mixing=20in=20biparti=
te.=20=20For=20instance,

I=20have=203=20actors,=20and=205=20organization.=20=20I=20am=20interested=20=
in=20whether=20Asian=20American=20is=20more=20likely=20to=20donate=20money=20=
to=20an=20Asian=20organization,=20Italian=20Americans=20to=20an=20Italian=20=
American=20organization,=20Irish=20American=20citizens=20to=20a=20Irish=20Am=
erican=20organization.=20=20(That=20is,=20issue=20on=20whether=20an=20actor'=
s=20attribute=20influences=20her=20choices=20of=20organization=20by=20its=20=
attributes.=20

I=20code=20Asian=3D1,=20Asian=20organization=3D1,=20Italian=20American=3D2,=20=
Italian=20American=20organization=3D2,=20Irish=20American=3D3,=20Irish=20org=
anization=3D3.

##Assume=20I=20had=20already=20recutangular=20edge=20lists=20file,=20and=20I=
=20first=20create=20bipartite=20network=20with=203=20actors=20and=205=20even=
ts.
mynet[,=202]<-mynet[,=202]+3
mynet<-network(mynet,=20bipartite=3D3,=20directed=3DF)

#I=20create=20actor=20attributes--(1)
ActorEthnic<-c(1,2,3,=20NA,=20NA,=20NA,=20NA,=20NA)
mynet<-set.vertex.attribute(mynet,=20"ActorEthnic",=20ActorEthnic)

##Then,=20I=20create=20organization=20attribute---(2)
OrgEthnic<-c(NA,=20NA,=20NA,=201,=202,=203,=201,=202)
mynet<-set.vertex.attribute(mynet,=20"OrgEthnic",=20OrgEthnic)

##Then,=20I=20create=20a=20COMBINED=20((1)+(2))attribute=20of
CombiEth<-c(1,=202,=203,=201,=202,=203,=201,=202)
mynet<-set.vertex.attribute(mynet,=20"CombiEth",=20CombiEth)

##Then,=20I=20ran=20my=20ergm.
model1<-ergm(mynet~edges+b1factor("ActorEthnic",=20base=3D1)+b2factor+("OrgE=
thnic",=20base=3D1)+nodematch("CombiEth",=20diff=3DT,=20keep=3Dc(1,=202,=203=
))
,=20seed=3D100)


Is=20this=20the=20right=20way=20to=20analyze=20the=20effects=20of=20selectiv=
e=20mixing=20between=20actors=20and=20events???

If=20wrong,=20please=20tell=20me=20the=20right=20and=20simple=20way=20to=20d=
o.

I=20look=20forward=20to=20hearing=20from=20somebody.

Megumi=20Nishimura
Ritsumeikan=20University
